detail: Between 10% and 20% below the high counts as a correction, and the S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 on Friday, about 11.6% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October. Corrections happen every year or two on average, and most do not turn into bear markets.
source: Reuters closing figures, 20 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was very narrow on Friday: on the Nasdaq 3,964 shares fell and only 928 rose, about 4.3 fallers for every riser, with 826 new 52-week lows against 21 new highs. When almost everything falls together, the selling is wide rather than limited to a few big names.

Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield fell to 4.92% on Friday as investors bought government bonds during the share sell-off. Safe bonds paying close to 5% still set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: The Closing Print closing levels, 20 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 96% on Friday, and traders saw about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: CME FedWatch via Reuters, 20 Nov; LSEG data via Reuters, 18 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, and Brent crude settled up 0.6% at $92.57 on Friday after new threats to shipping near Saudi Red Sea ports, though it fell for a third week. Dear oil keeps pressure on inflation, which is one reason central banks are raising rates.
source: ICE settlement via Reuters and EnergyNow, 20 Nov
